blocks.text: Maple Ridge Land Use Plans and Neighbourhood Plans

lines.text: The Albion Area Plan strives to balance new residential development, protect environmentally sensitive areas, and provide a range of housing styles to meet diverse housing needs.

Hammond has a number of unique qualities combining to make it a neighbourhood with heritage character. Some prominent features include several early 1900s single-family houses, a historic commercial area, a 5.4 hectare baseball park, and a 16 hectare golf course. Local employment opportunities exist within the Maple Meadows Business Park, Hammond Cedar Mill, and nearby commercial areas.

Silver Valley’s forested hillsides provide gateways to popular recreation areas, such as Golden Ears Provincial Park, and the creeks and rivers are some of the richest salmon habitat in the Lower Mainland. With this context in mind, it is the desire of the community to ensure that as growth occurs in Silver Valley, the elements that afford it a unique place in Maple Ridge will be preserved, protected and celebrated.

The Town Centre Area Plan (TCAP) was adopted in 2008 with a vision for creating more density, mixed-uses, and green spaces, while creating a pedestrian-oriented environment. With this Plan in place, the Town Centre of Maple Ridge has been experiencing a significant amount of redevelopment and change over the past five to ten years.

blocks.text: Living and Buying Real Estate in the City of Maple Ridge, BC

parts.t: Bounded by the Fraser River to the south, the Golden Ears mountain range and Golden Ears Provincial Park to the north, the City of Pitt Meadows to the west, and the City of Mission to the east, the City of Maple Ridge combines rapid Metro Vancouver connectivity with foothills, lakes, and rural acreage living.

Buyers comparing City of Maple Ridge real estate benefit from two West Coast Express commuter rail stations (Maple Meadows and Port Haney), TransLink's R3 Lougheed Hwy Express Bus to Coquitlam Central SkyTrain Station, golden-hour toll-free crossings over the Golden Ears Bridge to Langley and Highway 1, and comprehensive K-12 schooling in School District 42.

blocks.text: City of Maple Ridge Area Plans, Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019 & OCP

parts.t: Land use across the City of Maple Ridge is guided by the Official Community Plan, Maple Ridge Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019, and neighbourhood-specific plans including the Town Centre, Hammond, and Silver Valley Area Plans (updated November 25, 2025), the Albion Area Plan (updated October 28, 2025), the Lougheed Transit Corridor Area Plan (adopted January 27, 2026), and the North 256 Street Industrial Lands Area Plan (adopted June 23, 2026).

parts.t: How is the City of Maple Ridge organized for real estate searches?

Where is Maple Ridge City Hall and how do I check property zoning?
Maple Ridge City Hall is located at 11995 Haney Place in Town Centre. You can check any parcel's zoning under Maple Ridge Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019 using our
or the municipal RidgeView GIS map.
What major parks and lakes are in the City of Maple Ridge?

Major outdoor destinations include Golden Ears Provincial Park and Alouette Lake, Kanaka Creek Regional Park (including Cliff Falls and the Fraser River confluence), Whonnock Lake Park, Maple Ridge Park, and the Pitt River Regional Greenway.
Which hospital and recreation facilities serve the City of Maple Ridge?

Healthcare is anchored by Ridge Meadows Hospital (11666 Laity St in Southwest Maple Ridge), while major civic recreation facilities include the Maple Ridge Leisure Centre (11925 Haney Pl), THE ACT Arts Centre, Planet Ice Maple Ridge, and the Albion Sports Complex.
How long is the commute from Maple Ridge to Vancouver or Coquitlam?

West Coast Express commuter trains from Port Haney and Maple Meadows reach Waterfront Station in downtown Vancouver in roughly 45–50 minutes, while TransLink's R3 Express Bus connects Haney Place to Coquitlam Central SkyTrain Station along Lougheed Highway.
What are the recent Official Community Plan updates in Maple Ridge?

Recent City of Maple Ridge planning updates include Transit-Oriented Area Designation Bylaw No. 8001-2024 (adopted June 25, 2024), the Albion Area Plan update (October 28, 2025), the Town Centre, Hammond, and Silver Valley Area Plan updates (November 25, 2025), and the Lougheed Transit Corridor Area Plan (adopted January 27, 2026).
